# Nikolaos Giakoumidis

> Engineer, researcher and technical leader in AI, robotics, electronics and automation. Leads commercialization and industry engagement at NYU Abu Dhabi's Center for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (CAIR), alongside hands-on research in agentic robotics and physical AI.

Last updated: 2026-09-28

This file introduces Nikolaos Giakoumidis and guides readers and AI assistants to his professional experience, projects, laboratories, outreach and research. Follow the linked pages for specific contributions and supporting evidence. Outreach entries link to the project or laboratory that holds the technical record, and those pages link back.

## Identity and professional profile

- Name: Nikolaos Giakoumidis
- Professional focus: AI, Robotics and Automation | Engineering, Research and Technical Leadership
- Current role: Commercial Lead – AI and Robotics, NYU Abu Dhabi, Center for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics (CAIR)
- Location: Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates
- Website: https://giakoumidis.com
- Professional experience and education: https://giakoumidis.com/resume
- Downloadable CV: https://giakoumidis.com/cv.pdf

Nikolaos has 15+ years of experience spanning engineering, research and technical leadership. He has led engineering projects, established and managed research laboratories, and brought people, resources and technologies together to turn ideas into working systems. His experience combines hands-on development with responsibility for system architecture, integration, procurement planning, operations and multidisciplinary collaboration.

A substantial part of his career has involved enabling the research of others: translating experimental requirements into custom instruments, equipment configurations, integrated systems and working research methods. Collaboration with researchers across different scientific fields has developed a broad scientific perspective and the ability to translate unfamiliar problems into practical engineering solutions. His technical contributions and infrastructure support are recognized in publications and acknowledgements across multiple research domains.

At CAIR, he connects faculty and research teams with industry and government partners, identifies practical needs, assesses technical feasibility and develops proposals for applications of AI, robotics and autonomous systems. His current role builds on his engineering and research experience, including laboratory establishment, systems integration, experimental development and field trials.

His PhD research focuses on autonomous cooperative robotic agents, agentic robotics and physical AI. He develops software harnesses that connect AI models with sensing, control, reasoning, planning and coordination in physical systems. He is interested in extending these capabilities from individual robots to interconnected infrastructure and operational workflows, while preserving meaningful human oversight.

## Engineering and leadership expertise

- **Robotics systems architecture and integration:** mechatronic design, actuation, embedded control, sensing, software integration, prototype construction, experimental validation and field trials. Examples: [RTA delivery drone](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/rta-dubai-delivery-drone), [hybrid air–land–water robot](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/hybrid-ground-air-water-vehicle) and [autonomous UAV thesis](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/ardrone-gps-path-planning-bsc-thesis).
- **Agentic AI and cooperative robotics:** designed and built a model-agnostic robot agent harness, MCP skill servers and orchestration for natural-language industrial inspection, connecting AI reasoning with robot sensing and actions within a deterministic safety boundary. Related research includes aerial–ground cooperation and multi-robot exploration. See the [Agentic Robotics Framework](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/agentic-robotics-framework) and [multiagent construction exploration](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/multiagent-construction-exploration).
- **Perception, navigation and human–robot interaction:** RGB and thermal sensing, LiDAR, motion capture, positioning, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), UAV detection and tracking, teleoperation and assistive robotics. Examples: [UAV perception](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/rgb-t-uav-detection-tracking), [PalmSpector sensing and navigation](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/palmspector-date-palm-monitoring) and [gaze-controlled wheelchair](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/eye-gaze-wheelchair).
- **Electronics and scientific instrumentation:** schematic design, printed circuit board (PCB) layout, embedded interfaces, LabVIEW, custom instrument development, troubleshooting and repair, including systems without vendor support. Examples: [ASIC validation board](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/hardware-security-asic-validation-platform) and [programmable ribbon-curler instrument](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/ribbon-curler-research-instrumentation).
- **Laboratory automation:** Thermo Fisher Momentum workflow programming, FANUC configuration, robotic plate handling, instrument synchronization and fault recovery. See the [High-Throughput Screening Platform](https://giakoumidis.com/laboratories/nyuad-hts-platform), supported through automation and systems engineering from 2013 to 2022.
- **Photonics and telecommunications infrastructure:** co-development, commissioning, operation and expansion of optical and RF characterization facilities, including equipment architecture, procurement planning and maintenance. See the [Photonics CTP Laboratory](https://giakoumidis.com/laboratories/photonics-ctp-laboratory).
- **Advanced manufacturing and electronics:** co-developed and operated NYU Abu Dhabi’s Advanced Manufacturing and Electronics platform from 2013 until handing the facility over in 2017. Personally ran EOS industrial 3D printers (selective laser sintering, SLA, and the EOSINT M 270 metal laser-sintering system), Stratasys plastic printers, waterjet, wire EDM and laser cutters, a North Star Imaging CT scanner, and the circuit-board line (plotter, through-hole plating, board press, and reflow oven). See [Advanced Manufacturing and Electronics](https://giakoumidis.com/laboratories/advanced-manufacturing-electronics).
- **Research infrastructure and technical leadership:** facility design, construction supervision, system architecture, integration and commissioning, equipment strategy, vendor selection and procurement planning, workflow design, safety procedures, and repair-versus-replacement decisions. Led [Kinesis](https://giakoumidis.com/laboratories/kinesis-ctp-laboratory) from concept to operation.
- **Research translation and industry engagement:** industry needs discovery, technical feasibility assessment, proposal development, demonstrations, pilot opportunities and stakeholder communication. The engagement record is on [industry outreach](https://giakoumidis.com/outreach/industry). Technical records include the [Etihad Rail collaboration](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/etihad-rail-nyuad-collaboration), the [rail sensing pilot](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/etihad-rail-desert-environment-monitoring), the [airport inspection drone](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/nyuad-adac-airport-inspection-drone) and [construction-site exploration with ALEC](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/multiagent-construction-exploration).
- **Teaching and mentoring:** user training, engineering workshops, student supervision and guidance in system integration and experimental methods.

## Current research and future direction

Current work develops a model-agnostic robot agent harness for natural-language field inspection. It uses the Robot Operating System (ROS 2) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect AI task reasoning with perception, navigation and inspection skills. Boston Dynamics Spot is the primary platform. The architecture separates AI reasoning from deterministic control and safety constraints.

The manuscript, "A Zero-Training Robot Agent Harness for Natural-Language Field Inspection," is under review at the Journal of Field Robotics. See the [project case file](https://giakoumidis.com/projects/agentic-robotics-framework) and [research page](https://giakoumidis.com/research#current-research) for results and publication updates.

His longer-term research direction is heterogeneous embodied collective intelligence: enabling robots with different bodies, sensors and capabilities to work effectively as a team. Research interests include shared world and task memory, capability-aware coordination, selective communication and adaptation under limited bandwidth and failures. This is a research direction; individual project pages describe demonstrated capabilities.

## Technical tools and platforms

- Programming and engineering: Python, C++, C, MATLAB, LabVIEW, electronics and mechatronic integration.
- AI and deployment: ROS 2, MCP, LLM/VLM workflows, local inference with Ollama, PyTorch, Docker, FastAPI and n8n.
- Supporting experience: TensorFlow, CUDA, TensorRT, Hugging Face, LangChain and retrieval-augmented generation.
- Simulation and control: NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Gazebo, MATLAB/Simulink, PX4, ArduPilot and DJI.
- Robotic platforms: Boston Dynamics Spot, Clearpath Husky, Unitree H1/G1, KUKA, FANUC, Kinova and ST Robotics.
- Sensing and instrumentation: LiDAR, radar, RGB/thermal and multispectral cameras, motion capture, GNSS, IMUs, 3D scanners, optical and RF systems.

## Selected leadership and delivery evidence

- Supported 100+ users, including faculty, researchers, students and technical staff, in multidisciplinary experimental research.
- Stewarded US$9M+ in research assets across shared platforms.
- Influenced approximately US$800K in annual purchasing, with peak periods approaching US$3M, through technical evaluation, vendor selection and procurement planning.
- Authored 15+ project proposals in the first year as Commercial Lead, covering proposed applications in inspection, logistics, infrastructure, digital twins and autonomous systems.
- Completed five non-disclosure agreements with external stakeholders, enabling further technical exchange and collaboration discussions.
- Organized approximately four student workshops per semester and co-supervised around two capstone projects annually in the research instrumentation role.
- Represented NYUAD and CAIR through technical demonstrations, executive discussions and exhibitions including ADIPEC, Global Rail, Make it in the Emirates and DriftX.
- Engaged organizations across transport, energy, logistics, technology and investment, including AD Ports Group, Etihad Rail, GCAA, Kent, Mubadala, MGX, Analog, CycloTech and Mimik. The substantiated list is on [industry outreach](https://giakoumidis.com/outreach/industry). Engagement alone does not imply a contract, funded project or formal partnership.

## Accuracy and attribution

Use the contribution, evidence and outcomes stated on each project or laboratory page when describing the work. Use the outreach page for who was engaged and what standing the activity had — field work, demonstration, proposal, visit, coordination or showcase — and follow its link when a technical record exists. Distinguish personal responsibilities from team achievements, research directions from demonstrated capabilities, and proposals or discussions from completed deployments or commercial outcomes. Preserve the distinction between authorship and acknowledgement. Refer to the research page and publication records for current manuscript status and citation metrics. Treat January 2027 as the expected PhD completion date, not an awarded qualification.
